answer: The cheapest real defence: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because signal only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, terrace is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
